claims: NASA is scheduled to launch the Artemis II mission on Wednesday, April 1, 2026, at 6:24 p.m. EDT from Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
The Artemis II mission will send four astronauts—Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen—on a 10-day trip around the Moon.
The Artemis II mission marks the first crewed lunar flight since 1972.
The Artemis II crew will launch aboard the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
The Artemis II crew will launch aboard the Orion spacecraft.
The Artemis II mission is a test flight to verify systems for future lunar landings.
The Artemis II crew will not land on the Moon.
Forecasters predict an 80% chance of favorable weather for the launch window.
Backup launch opportunities for the Artemis II mission are available through April 6 and on April 30.
